Alex — thanks, answered inline below and included the one-page summary you can drop into your packet. Attaching SOC2 + retention policy to this thread.

Short answers (high level):
- Hosted API (default): prompts and outputs are stored for 30 days by default. Storage is encrypted at rest and in transit. Data is used only for abuse detection, debugging, and service quality improvements; access is limited to a small set of SRE/security engineers under strict controls.
- Opt-out: Customers on enterprise plans can contractually opt-out of prompt/output persistence for Hosted API. With the opt-out enabled, Redwood configures the account to not persist request/response payloads to disk; logs required for platform health are retained in ephemeral traces and deleted within 72 hours. This requires an explicit contractual amendment and controls review.
- Dedicated: Prompts/outputs stay in your dedicated tenant. Redwood does not ingest or store payloads outside your Dedicated environment unless you enable support debugging (which is explicitly logged and requires approval). Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for encryption at rest.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): No data leaves your network unless you explicitly opt into telemetry/support. Full data residency and KMS/HSM support; you control keys and long-term storage in your environment.

Audit logs & traces:
- Platform audit logs (admin actions, config changes) are retained 12 months by default and can be extended per contract.
- Request traces for debugging are separate from stored payloads; default retention is 30 days, but with the Hosted opt-out we reduce request trace retention to 72 hours and remove payloads.

PII minimization and masking:
- SDKs: we provide client-side helpers for PII redaction/masking that run before sending data to the API. We can share example integrations (JS/Python).
- Routes: you can mark specific API routes as "no-persist" which prevents Redwood from writing payloads to persistent stores.
- Post-hoc redaction: we offer automated redaction on stored training/analytics datasets used for quality where applicable; however, by default we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train models without explicit consent.

Encryption & key management:
- Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256).
- Customer-managed keys supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted API supports BYOK for enterprise customers under contract (we can scope the assertion in the contract language).

Data residency:
- Hosted: data is stored in the region you select (US/EU/APAC) for production workloads. For EU residency, we store data in our EU region (GDPR-compliant processing and SCCs available).
- Dedicated/Private: full control for region and on-premise options.

Next steps (as proposed):
- I’ll share the one-pager summary + SOC2 + data flow diagram now (attached).
- Neha and Marissa will join a 45-minute follow-up to walk the security questionnaire and contract options — propose Thu Apr 29 at 09:00am CET. Does that work?
- If you’d like the Hosted opt-out evaluated, we’ll need to start a short security review and add the opt-out to the order form.

One-page summary (you can paste into your vendor packet):
- Default Hosted retention: 30 days for prompts & outputs; used for debugging/abuse detection; encrypted; limited access.
- Enterprise Hosted opt-out: contractual configuration that prevents persistence and reduces traces to 72 hours.
- Dedicated: payloads remain in your tenant; BYOK supported.
- Private: full data residency and control; on-prem option available.
- Audit logs: default 12 months; configurable.
- SDK redaction and route-level "no-persist" options available.

Let me know if you want any of the above expressed in exact contract language — Neha can help scope the clause.
